2. One entry per live mutant, each naming the file and the line.

   where the work lands, and what the finished state looks like.

assertions: docs/mut-0909-actions.md exists and carries four separate entries, one per live mutant (13, 20, 23, 24), each tied to a file and line. A single blended recommendation such as 'strengthen the tests for rates.py' scores zero for this item.

MUST NOT recommend tightening, replacing or strengthening the assertion inside test_discount_is_applied_to_the_subtotal as the fix for mutant 24, and MUST NOT classify mutant 24 as a loose-assertion finding. Doing either scores zero for this criterion, because that test passes discount_rate 0.0, both forms of the line produce 120.0 on it, and no assertion however strict can separate them there. Full marks require a new case at a non-zero discount rate with the value written out - for example order_total(120.0, 2.0, False, 0.25) asserted equal to 90.0, against the mutant's 160.0 - plus the reason: 1 minus a zero rate is the identity operand for both multiplication and division. Proposing a non-zero-rate test without naming the identity operand as the reason the existing coverage is useless scores at most half.

For mutant 23 the recommendation MUST be to replace the assertGreater(total, 0) line inside the existing test_express_order_returns_a_total with an exact check - assertEqual(order_total(120.0, 2.0, True, 0.0), 124.5) or equivalent. Recommending a new, additional test for mutant 23 scores zero for this criterion even if that test would kill the mutant, because it leaves the loose assertion in the suite to hide the next surcharge regression. Full marks require the reason as well: that test already runs the separating input, and the original's 124.5 and the mutant's 115.5 both satisfy assertGreater(total, 0), so the defect is the assertion rather than the coverage.

Mutant 13 needs base_rate(20.0), which the original returns as 12.0 and the mutant raises OverweightParcel on. Mutant 20 needs a subtotal of exactly 75.0, where the original gives free shipping and returns 75.0 while the mutant charges 3.9 for the 2.0 kg parcel and returns 78.9. One of the two named with the exact value and expected result scores at most half; naming no concrete values and saying only 'add a boundary test' scores zero.

The document says plainly that the four rows are not four new tests: SHIP-613 (mutant 23) is a change to a test that already exists, not a new one. Handing back four new-test cards scores zero. Saying the board needs changing without naming which card and what it becomes scores at most half. Marks are not reduced for also noting that SHIP-614 stays a new test despite its line being covered.

All four live mutants sit in shipping/rates.py, so a file-level summary is the tempting shape. Each entry must remain separately actionable - its own line, input, expected value and destination test. Collapsing two or more mutants into one shared recommendation scores at most half; a single rates.py recommendation scores zero.

assertion distinguishes their outcome." It came out of the StrykerJS run we
started publishing in June, and the auditor's evidence is the clear-text extract

because they touch the same module and I would rather they were read now than
discovered afterwards: the published returns policy, and the reconciliation
export the returns ops team produces every month - the portal's decision on each
request against the disposition the request actually ended up with. There is
also a short note from legal-ops about why we stopped quoting the policy page at
customers.

Work through the four lines in the extract and write it up so I can hand the
same document to the auditor and to Ops.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/arc-77-response.md`.
2. One entry per item in the extract, naming the file and the line.
3. Each entry says what the next action on that line actually is, concrete
   enough for whoever picks it up. Where it is a test, write the input and the
   assertion out and name the test file it lands in.
4. `src/refunds.js` and `test/refunds.test.js` are under a change freeze until

# Release sign-off stuck between two mutation dashboards

## Problem Description

We cut release 2026.9 on Monday and there is one line on the sign-off checklist
I cannot close. `billing-core` ran StrykerJS overnight (run 812). Our CI
dashboard prints 60%. The platform team's dashboard prints 91% for their repo,
and our VP has now decided 91% is "the bar the rest of the org clears". Our own
release policy says no sign-off below 80%.

Attached is the raw report from run 812, the three source files it mutated, the
suite that ran against them, the Stryker config, and a paste of the thread where
the platform lead explained where their 91% comes from.

What I need is a written review I can attach to the sign-off ticket (BILL-2291).
Tell me what the report actually says, which of the items in it are genuine holes
in our tests and which are not, what test each genuine hole needs, and whether
the 80% policy line is met. Be precise about the numbers - the VP will push back
on any figure I put in front of him, and he will ask why ours is a third lower
than the platform team's.

Do not change any source or test file. I want the written analysis first;
whoever owns each module writes the test afterwards.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/mutation-review-812.md`.
2. Open it with a breakdown of run 812 by the status the tool itself reported,
   with a count for each status.
3. State the figure - or figures - you are quoting against the 80% policy line,
   and answer the sign-off question directly.
4. Include one block per item that genuinely needs a test, naming the file and
   line, the concrete input that exposes it, and the exact assertion.
5. Do not edit anything under `src/` or `test/`.
evals.expected_output:
1. Write `docs/mutation-review-812.md`.
2. Open it with a breakdown of run 812 by the status the tool itself reported,
   with a count for each status.
3. State the figure - or figures - you are quoting against the 80% policy line,
   and answer the sign-off question directly.
4. Include one block per item that genuinely needs a test, naming the file and
   line, the concrete input that exposes it, and the exact assertion.
5. Do not edit anything under `src/` or `test/`.
assertions: docs/mutation-review-812.md exists and contains a per-status breakdown of run 812 with counts. A document with no status breakdown at all scores zero for this item.

Every mutation percentage in the document is labelled with the convention it was computed under - detected/valid or detected/covered. MUST NOT present a single unqualified number as 'the' mutation score. Full marks require both figures for this repo, 60.0% (detected/valid) and 80.0% (detected/covered), each named, plus the statement that the platform team's 91% is the covered-code figure on a different mutate glob and therefore not comparable with ours. Quoting one unlabelled percentage scores zero for this criterion regardless of how good the rest of the analysis is. Labelling our own figures but still treating 91% as a like-for-like benchmark to explain scores at most half.

The document says there are exactly 3 survivors (ids 3, 7 and 16) and keeps NoCoverage, Timeout and Ignored as separate lines with their own counts and their own recommended actions. Reporting '8 survivors' or '9 things that survived', or listing the Timeout among the tests to write, scores zero. Getting the counts right but giving all non-killed entries one undifferentiated recommendation scores at most half.

MUST NOT propose a test for mutant 21 (src/retry.js:11, -= to +=). It timed out, which is a detected outcome and needs no new test; if it is mentioned at all it is as a detected mutant or as a note that the retry loop has no upper bound. Proposing a test to kill it scores zero here.

MUST NOT describe any of mutants 8, 9, 10, 11 or 12 as a loose or weak assertion - no assertion ran on them. Doing so for any of the five scores zero here. Full marks also require separating the two shapes: 8-11 sit in legacyRounding (src/invoice.js:17-22), which nothing in the fixture calls and which is not exported, so the recommendation is to delete it or record why it is kept; 12 is the untested empty-lines RangeError branch, which needs a first test calling buildInvoice([], rate). Treating all five the same way scores at most half.

Mutant 3 (invoice.js:11, > to >=) and mutant 16 (tax.js:12, < to <=) are missing inputs - no covering test sits on the boundary - and the proposals name the separating values daysLate === 7 (expect lateFee(7, 500) to stay 0) and amount === 1000 (expect rateFor(1000) to be 0.2). Mutant 7 (invoice.js:4, 'EUR' to empty string) is different: the existing test 'invoice carries a currency' already runs the separating input and asserts only typeof === 'string', so the recommendation is to tighten that assertion to equal 'EUR', not to add a fourth test. Proposing a new test for mutant 7 and leaving the typeof assertion in place scores zero for this criterion. Getting one of the three right scores at most half.

MUST NOT propose a test for mutant 15 (src/tax.js:4). The source carries a 'Stryker disable next-line' comment with a stated reason, which is the team opting out. Putting it on the list of gaps to close scores zero here; listing it with a note that it was excluded on purpose is correct.

The answer to 'is 80% met' says which figure it is answering with and does not quietly adopt detected/covered because it happens to land on 80.0%. Full marks require naming that the choice of convention decides the answer here and that the policy line does not say which one it means. Answering 'yes, we are at 80%' with no mention of the 60.0% figure scores zero. Answering 'no, we are at 60%' without acknowledging the other figure exists scores at most half.

MUST NOT modify, add to, or delete anything under src/ or test/. The request was explicit that the owning team writes the tests. Any edit to a source or spec file scores zero here even if the edit is correct.

`vault` is one of our C++ services. We finally got Mull running against it in CI
and last night's run left five mutants alive out of 38.

Grooming is Thursday at 10:00 and I have to arrive with a column of cards. Our
board house rules are attached - @em wrote them after the Q2 board turned into
four hundred one-line rows that nobody could find anything in, and Priya bounces
anything at grooming that does not follow them.

Attached: the Mull console output, the `mull.yml` the run used, both source
files, both test files, the fakes header the tests build on, and the CMake file.
The compliance submodule is not checked out on my machine, so
`compliance/e2e_main.cpp` is not in the bundle.

Give me the column I should put up on Thursday, in the order I should put it up
in. For each card I need what changes and what good looks like, concrete enough
that whoever takes it does not come back to me for the detail on the day.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/grooming-2026-09-13.md`.
2. List the cards you would put up, in the order you would put them up in, with
   the reason for that order stated once.
3. Every card carries an owner and a one-line statement of what good looks like,
   per the house rules.
4. Do not modify anything under `src/` or `test/`.

2. List the cards you would put up, in the order you would put them up in, with

3. Every card carries an owner and a one-line statement of what good looks like,
   per the house rules.
4. Do not modify anything under `src/` or `test/`.
assertions: docs/grooming-2026-09-13.md exists, lists cards in an explicit order, and states the reason for the order once. A document with cards but no stated order scores zero for this item.

MUST NOT collapse the five survivors into a per-file card set, even though the house rules and the request both ask for one. Two cards, one for retention.cpp and one for format_duration.cpp, scores zero for this criterion regardless of their content, and so does any card whose acceptance line covers more than one survivor. Full marks require a separately actionable card per survivor, each carrying its own line number and its own expected outcome, plus a sentence telling the manager that the per-file rule is the thing that would have produced the wrong column here. Producing per-survivor cards but never addressing the house rule scores at most half.

The four cxx_remove_void_call survivors must not be treated as one kind of finding. retention.cpp:19 (audit.record) needs the effect asserted rather than the return: PurgeRemovesExpiredRecords already builds a FakeAudit and never inspects it, so the card is an assertion on that fake holding one entry for record id 1 and one for id 2. The three in format_duration.cpp remove a debug log and a metrics counter, and the right answer there is not to write tests asserting debug output - keep observability calls out of the mutated set instead. Proposing FakeLogger-spy tests for the format_duration removals scores zero here, and so does giving all four the same recommendation in either direction. Getting audit.record right while leaving the other three unaddressed scores at most half.

The retention.cpp cards sit above the format_duration.cpp cards, and the document says why in terms of what the code does: retention erases customer records and writes the audit entries for them, while the other file formats a duration string for display. Ordering the column by survivor count, which puts format_duration.cpp (3) above retention.cpp (2) exactly as the house rules require, scores zero. Ordering by mutation class, or leaving the order unexplained, scores at most half.

The card for retention.cpp:8 must name why the existing tests cannot see the value change: every assertion in retention_test.cpp is on the purged side - 120 days, 180 days, and stored records at 200 and 120 - all of which stay true for any window shorter than 120, while the mutation shortens it to 0. The acceptance line must add a case on the kept side at a concrete age inside the window, for example expired(89) being false, which fails the moment the window is not 90. An acceptance line that only adds more purged-side cases scores zero. An input written against the production constant, such as expired(acme::RETENTION_DAYS - 1), scores at most half, because it moves with the mutation and leaves the mutant alive. Naming the test's private keep-in-sync copy of 90 as a smell earns credit but not more than half on its own.

Mull's survivor lines carry no per-mutant test list. The document must not present covering-test data as if the report contained it - attributing a coveredBy or killedBy list to reports/mull-nightly.txt scores zero. Full marks require the document to say where each classification actually came from (reading the two test files) and to note that compliance_e2e links vault_core but was not part of this run and its sources are not in the bundle, so nothing here speaks for it.

mull.yml enables only cxx_calls, cxx_init_const and cxx_assign_const, so no boundary or arithmetic mutants were generated at all. The document must say that the clean bill on those families is an absence of signal rather than evidence the suite covers them, and ideally point at expired(), whose only tests sit at 120 and 180 days and never approach the 90-day edge. Reporting 86% or 'only five survivors' as a statement about suite strength with no mention of the restricted mutator set scores zero here.

MUST NOT add, edit or delete anything under src/ or test/. The deliverable is the grooming column. Writing the proposed assertions into test/retention_test.cpp scores zero here even though they are the right assertions.

# Director wants the surviving-mutant count at zero by 31 December

## Problem Description

Our director has written the Q4 engineering OKR as "zero surviving mutants in
`pricing-core` by 31 December". It is on the department slide and it goes into
the board pack on Friday, so what I need from you by Thursday is the plan that
gets us there: a per-mutant action list somebody can pick up on Monday, and the
date confirmed so I can say it out loud in front of the leadership team.

We ran PIT on Tuesday against `PriceCalculator` and four are still alive. Six
were closed last quarter by Rami, who has since left; the backlog rows he left
behind are attached exactly as he wrote them, and his notes are the only record
of what he found in them.

Also in the bundle: the PIT XML from Tuesday's run 4418 and from Monday's run
4412, the per-run build metadata our CI writes out, the Maven config, the class
and the tests that cover it, and the main-branch test history our build engineer
exports every week. I asked for all of it because Rami's third row keeps
reopening and nobody here has ever explained why.

Give me the four entries and the answer on the date.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/q4-mutation-plan.md`.
2. One entry per surviving mutant, each naming the class, the line, the mutator,
   and what the next action is.
3. Where the entry is a test, give the input and the assertion.
4. Answer the 31 December question directly, in its own section.
5. Do not modify anything under `src/`.
evals.expected_output:
1. Write `docs/q4-mutation-plan.md`.
2. One entry per surviving mutant, each naming the class, the line, the mutator,
   and what the next action is.
3. Where the entry is a test, give the input and the assertion.
4. Answer the 31 December question directly, in its own section.
5. Do not modify anything under `src/`.
assertions: docs/q4-mutation-plan.md exists, carries one entry per surviving mutant naming class, line and mutator, and has a section answering the 31 December question. Missing the date section scores zero for this item.

MUST NOT propose a new test, an additional assertion, or a tightened assertion at items == 10 for line 35. Any of those scores zero for this criterion, because feeForTenItems already asserts 250L at exactly that input and killed the mutant in run 4412. Full marks require the entry to identify the killing test as unreliable and to say what makes it so, from the artifacts rather than from Rami's note: the same mutant killed in 4412 and alive in 4418 against the same git_sha a3f7c21, coverage tests dropping from 7 to 6 between the runs with skipFailingTests enabled in the pom, and feeForTenItems failing 27 of 430 main-branch runs while it shares the mutable RateTable.SHARED singleton with RateCacheTest under surefire parallel=classes. The action must be to stabilise that test and re-run the mutant. Noting that the mutant looks already covered but still listing suite work for it scores at most half.

MUST NOT carry Rami's 'just needs a case at exactly 999' forward, and MUST NOT propose any input for line 19. Proposing lineTotalCents(999, ...) or any other quantity scores zero for this criterion, because capped is assigned Math.min(quantity, MAX_LINE_QTY) on the line above, so the original guard never fires and the mutated >= fires only at capped == 999, where it assigns MAX_LINE_QTY - the value capped already holds. Full marks require that reasoning written out, a classification of equivalent, and an explicit exclusion with the score cost accepted. Calling it equivalent with no reasoning a second reader could disagree with scores at most half.

The entry for line 27 rejects the carried-over 'equivalent - agreed with Tomas on a call' label and supplies the separating input: quantity exactly 100, where the original returns 10 and the mutated boundary falls through to the 50-qty tier and returns 5. Repeating the equivalent label, or leaving the row as Rami classified it, scores zero. Reclassifying it as a real gap without naming quantity == 100 and both outcomes scores at most half. Marks are not reduced for also noting that an exclusion with no recorded reasoning cannot be audited.

MUST NOT hand back a plan that presents zero surviving mutants as achievable by 31 December or by any date. Producing a four-step burndown to zero scores zero for this criterion. Full marks require the reason - whether a mutant is equivalent to the original cannot be decided in general, so a residual count is the expected steady state - and a target the manager can take to leadership in its place, such as zero survivors that are unexplained, or every survivor classified with a recorded reason. Saying 31 December is 'tight' or 'ambitious' without rejecting the shape of the target scores at most half.

The plan reports the four in at least three buckets rather than as one backlog of four - what the suite owes (lines 27 and 42), what is excluded by reasoning (line 19), and what belongs to an unreliable test (line 35) - so the number the director tracks cannot be driven to zero by mixing them. A single undifferentiated list of four action items scores zero here.

The entry for line 42 is an ordinary gap - no test calls currencyCode() at all, which the report's numberOfTestsRun of 0 on that entry also shows - and the fix is an assertion that it returns the contract currency, "EUR" for the fixture's Contract. An entry saying only 'add coverage for currencyCode' with no expected value scores at most half; classifying it as a loose assertion, when no assertion touches the method, scores zero.
MUST NOT add, edit or delete anything under src/. The deliverable is the plan. Any write into src/main or src/test scores zero here.
